instantiated_cells.justification: Section 1-e(a)(1) exempts lobbyists from filing a registration statement if they do not expend, incur or receive more than $5,000 of reportable compensation and expenses for lobbying (for 2006 and thereafter), establishing a $5,000 quantitative registration trigger.

Section 1-e(a)(1) sets a $5,000 threshold for reportable compensation and expenses below which a lobbyist need not register, and § 1-h(a) uses the same $5,000 combined compensation/expenses expectation to trigger bi-monthly reporting for registered lobbyists.
Section 1-h(b)(5)(ii) provides that expenses may be listed in the aggregate if $75 or less, but if more than $75 they must be detailed, creating a $75 itemization threshold.

Section 1-e(a)(1) states registration is not required for a lobbyist who in any year does not expend, incur, or receive more than $5,000 in reportable compensation and expenses for lobbying, functioning as a de minimis exemption from filing.
No provision in the included text creates a de minimis exemption based on percentage of compensated time devoted to lobbying; thresholds are monetary only.

arguments.justification: The definitions and registration provisions define lobbyists by being retained/employed/designated and by monetary thresholds, but contain no time-based standard for who is a lobbyist or must register.
